stories.title: The US and Israel are reported to be planning new strikes on Iran after the midterms
stories.summary: NPR spoke with retired Gen. Joseph Votel about a US and Israeli plan for a possible bombing campaign after the US [[midterms|midterm elections]], and France 24 reports that the New York Times has described plans for fresh strikes. Al Jazeera says emergency oil stocks are at multidecade lows, and analysts quoted there say the world may have only a month or two of cover if the [[strait-of-hormuz|Strait of Hormuz]] shuts again.
stories.background: The US and Israel launched a war on Iran on 28 February 2026. A ceasefire has not held: Iran has blocked the Strait of Hormuz and targeted commercial ships, and the US has blockaded Iranian ports and oil shipments.

sources.title: Retired general discusses the U.S. and Israeli plan for possible attack on Iran
NYT reports plans for fresh strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections
Are global oil reserves sufficient to withstand renewed US-Iran war?

stories.title: France plans to deploy 70,000 security officers as Macron meets students before new protests
stories.summary: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 70,000 security forces will be mobilised for protests across France on Saturday, as President Emmanuel Macron met student representatives for the first time. Macron said on Thursday that 'illegitimate' protests would be banned and blamed 'seditious' ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's riots and looting. Authorities are also asking the public to hand in videos of looting to help identify rioters, a move France 24 says has caused debate.
stories.background: The protests followed a wave of anger over the cost of living, and the government has imposed curfews in several cities to prevent more violence. Young people have also protested in other countries, which commentators on Al Jazeera and France 24 link to inequality and weak public services.

sources.title: Live: France will deploy 70,000 security forces for Saturday protests, says interior minister
French authorities call for videos of looting to identify rioters
Macron to meet student groups: Where are France’s protests heading?

stories.title: Putin says Russia will resume three-way talks, but wants a final deal rather than a truce
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that Russia is ready to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the US, but on the security terms of a final peace deal and not on a 'short' ceasefire. Separately, France 24 reports that Donald Trump said Ukraine's access to the [[starshield|Starshield]] satellite system had been restored after Kyiv reported limits, while US officials and allies have blamed each other for the problem.
stories.background: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. The last US-mediated talks were in February 2026, just before the US and Israel went to war with Iran.

sources.title: Russia ready for talks on plans for final Ukraine deal, not truce: Putin
US offers mixed messages on limits to Ukraine's Starshield system

stories.title: Israel orders the army to prepare a full closure of the West Bank after a deadly gunfight
stories.summary: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men near Hebron on Friday who the military said had launched an attack, and at least five people were injured, some critically, NPR reports. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office told the army to prepare a full closure of the occupied [[west-bank|West Bank]], according to France 24. Al Jazeera says the clampdown comes as attacks on Palestinian farmers are increasing.
stories.background: Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. France 24 notes the attack comes before an Israeli election.

sources.title: Israel orders closure of West Bank after soldiers kill 2 men behind an alleged attack
Netanyahu orders army to prepare for full West Bank closure after attack
Israel preparing full lockdown of occupied West Bank after Hebron gunfight

stories.title: South Korea invites North Korea to military talks to calm rising border tension
stories.summary: Seoul said it has invited Pyongyang to talks about restoring military communication lines and preventing accidental clashes. The offer came days after North Korea said it had moved new military units into 'firing positions' along the border. It is unclear whether Pyongyang will agree.
stories.background: Al Jazeera says North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has taken a hardline approach to Seoul and suspended virtually all dialogue and cooperation with the South in recent years.

sources.title: South Korea invites North for military talks over border

stories.title: Serbia votes on Sunday in a snap election that tests a student-led challenge to Vucic
stories.summary: The 25 October parliamentary vote will show whether President Aleksandar Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party can extend its 14-year hold on power or whether a student-led movement can loosen it, Al Jazeera reports. Vucic resigned the presidency in September and is leading his party's campaign for prime minister.
stories.background: In November 2024 the collapse of a concrete canopy at a railway station in Novi Sad killed 16 people. Demands for accountability grew into a nationwide movement against alleged corruption, with students as its driving force.

sources.title: Serbia’s snap election: What’s at stake and can students unseat Vucic?

France 24 says Flavio Bolsonaro, son of ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, beat Lula by a small margin in the first round.

stories.title: A grenade exercise sparked the deadly fire at a Canadian military base, the army says
stories.summary: A fire that killed four soldiers at the Wainwright base in Alberta was sparked by an exercise using live grenades, a military official said. High winds pushed the blaze across the base, and a later change in wind direction made it much fiercer. Firefighters could not fight it directly because it was in the range's permanent danger area.

stories.title: Europe enters winter with its lowest gas reserves on record, the IEA chief warns
stories.summary: Fatih Birol, head of the International Energy Agency, told Al Jazeera that Europe is entering winter with historically low gas stocks and cannot withstand further supply shocks as the Iran war disrupts global energy supplies. He said Europe will likely face rising costs for liquefied natural gas in the coming months even if peace returned to the Gulf today.
